prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and quantum spin Hall effect, and the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B048 as my preferred configuration and I have not changed it since round 1; what has changed is that I now put its attribution problem at the centre of my argument and not at the edge. Kane and Mele introduced the Z2 invariant and the time-reversal-protected quantum spin Hall state, which classified band insulators by topology without a magnetic field, and Molenkamp's group delivered the first transport observation of helical edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells. That is a complete prediction-to-confirmation arc, confirmed independently for about two decades with transport, ARPES and scanning probes, and no longer controversial. Four members now name it first and the chair's summary shows that B016 and B049 members themselves list it as an alternative, which tells me it is the position most members can live with. I treat that as a tie-breaker between close scientific cases, not as the argument itself. The argument is the concept: a new organising principle for electronic matter, tested by a decisive experiment. I also keep my own circuit QED candidate (B038) out of the configuration for two reasons that I think are scientific as much as personal: it follows the 2025 prize in a neighbouring part of superconducting-circuit physics, and its credit cannot be fitted into three names without leaving out one of Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf or Wallraff.
statement.case_against: The BHZ gap is real and I will not pretend a citation closes it. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang identified HgTe quantum wells with an inverted band structure as the concrete realisation, and the three-dimensional topological insulator work (Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents, Hasan and Cava) is a separate large body of credit. A three-person prize cannot cover all of this. I accept the risk that a careful reader will say the prize draws a line through a crowded history. In addition, the 2016 prize covers neighbouring topological ground, and the overlap with B016 in vocabulary is real, even if the physics differs. If the committee concludes that the BHZ role was a necessary part of the discovery, rather than a refinement of a prediction already made by Kane and Mele, then B048 is weaker than the tidier B049 and I would move to B049 before B016.

responses.point: Mehlig moved from B041 to B048, called the BHZ omission the main attribution problem, and named B016 as the cleaner theory-plus-experiment triple if the attribution cannot be resolved within three names.
responses.response: I agree we have reached the same place from different starting points, and I take the B016 comparison seriously. On attribution, B016 is not as clean as it looks: Cao, Fatemi and the 2018 experimental team are outside Jarillo-Herrero's name, and earlier continuum-model work sits outside Bistritzer and MacDonald, so B016 also draws a contestable line. The difference is in the kind of omission. For B048 the missing step (BHZ) is a material-specific prediction that refined an already-stated quantum spin Hall prediction, while Molenkamp's measurement is directly the observation of that state. I would accept a citation that names the Z2 state and its first observation in HgTe and says nothing broader, and I would regard a citation claiming credit for topological insulators in general as disqualifying, because it would include the 3D work that these three names do not cover.

responses.point: Pearce, the chair, prefers B016 because a specific quantitative prediction (Bistritzer-MacDonald) was followed by a decisive experiment, with broad reproduction, and accepts the unsettled pairing mechanism and about seven years of confirmation.
responses.response: The Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction followed by the 2018 experiment is a strong arc and I do not dispute the reproducibility. My difference is on maturity. For twisted bilayer graphene the committee would be honouring the existence of correlated insulators and superconductivity while the pairing mechanism and the nature of the insulating states remain open, about seven years after the experiments. For B048 the interpretation has been stable for two decades. I would not argue that seven years is too short in itself, since prizes have been awarded on shorter timescales, but when two candidates have comparable theory-plus-experiment structure I would take the one whose interpretation has stopped moving. I also note that your own case_against lists topological insulators as more mature than B016, so I think we agree on that fact and weigh it differently. If the committee chooses B016 I would support a citation limited, as the chair's round-1 question suggests, to the flat-band prediction and the discovery of the correlated and superconducting states, with no mechanism claim.

responses.point: Lindroth keeps optical lattice clocks first, rejecting my earlier worry that this is engineering, and says the magic-wavelength condition is a physics insight and the 1e-18 level comparisons test relativity directly.
responses.response: I accept your correction: I had framed B049 too much as the best implementation of the 2005 and 2012 toolkit, and the magic-wavelength condition, which removes the differential light shift for many atoms in a lattice, is a new principle. I therefore keep B049 as an alternative and would rank it above B038 as a fallback. What keeps me with B048 is not novelty but two other points. First, you yourself note that Katori's priority over other early lattice-clock proposers is resting on recalled history, and I cannot resolve that from the record either. Second, the redefinition of the second has not happened, so the strongest practical consequence is still pending. If the committee judges that B048's BHZ tangle is not repairable, I would support Katori and Ye without hesitation, since the two-name credit is the cleanest on the shortlist.

responses.point: Olsson, who ranked B048 first, said the citation should rest on the conceptual advance and not on promised applications, and insisted the three names be justified on the record.
responses.response: I agree and I have written the citation accordingly: it names the Z2 state, the quantum spin Hall effect and the HgTe observation, and does not mention topological quantum computing or devices. On justifying the three names, my argument is this. Kane and Mele are the originators of the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall prediction. Molenkamp is the person whose group first observed the state and showed the helical edge transport, with the 2007 conductance quantisation in HgTe wells. The three names are not justified by forming a tidy trio but by each holding a role that the citation text names. I do not claim this settles the BHZ question and I would rather the committee record that as a stated limit of the citation.

uncertainties: Whether the BHZ HgTe proposal was an essential step or a refinement of the Kane-Mele prediction; I rely on recalled history that I cannot verify here, and a different judgement would move me to B049.

Whether the 2016 topological-phases prize reduces B048's priority more than I currently think; I distinguish the Z2 time-reversal-invariant case from the quantum Hall and defect-transition work of 2016, but others do not.
Whether seven years of confirmation for B016 is enough once the pairing mechanism remains open, and whether I am weighting maturity too heavily against a candidate with the broadest opening support.
Whether Katori's priority among early lattice-clock proposers is settled, which determines how much of B049's clean credit I can rely on.
statement.conflict_note: I have a possible conflict on B038 (circuit QED): I am a theorist in superconducting circuits and microwave quantum optics at Chalmers, direct WACQT, and am a colleague of Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson. B038 is not in my preferred configuration or alternatives, so I do not seek recusal, but I would discount my own view and ask the committee to do the same if B038 is brought back. I also have a documented collaborator in Anton Frisk Kockum, with no recorded link to the credited names in B048, B016 or B049. No specific personal or institutional connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer, Katori or Ye is apparent from my profile.
